We had the whole place to ourselves, which made the experience even better.We started by cooking Indian banana leaf curry rice and enjoyed some delicious payasam for dessert. Later in the evening, we prepared Korean steamboat for dinner, played UNO cards, and even danced the night away. The room was pleasantly cold even without turning on the fan, and the linens were clean and fresh.The next morning, we cooked breakfast and enjoyed the amazing waterfall shower—it was such a refreshing experience. The waterfall itself is beautiful and serene. For lunch, we cooked again, and during that time, we noticed a group of motorbikes and some Singaporean cars entering the area. They stayed for about an hour to shower and then left.We eventually left in the evening, feeling incredibly satisfied. This time, having the entire waterfall to ourselves made the trip unforgettable. It truly felt like the whole place belonged to us! Highly recommend this unique experience.

Title: Air Terjun Takah Pengkoi
Review: This campsite/waterfall is located in Segamat district, Johor. Nearest town from Takah Pengkoi is Bekok town. You can get supplies here before entering the oil palm plantation where the campsite is located. Bear in mind there is very limited phone signal at the campsite. To get there, it is most convenient to locate Sekolah Kebangsaan Kampung Kudong then go pass it till you find the Takah Pengkoi sign board on your left. Turn left, go straight and you will arrive at the entrance of the campsite. Register and pay for the entrance fee. There is a kak Ros there who does the registration. Fees cost RM40 per pax per night, or RM70 per pax for 2 nights or RM15 per pax for day trip. Operation hours 9am to 7pm. The campsite parking can fit in 20-30 cars. Otherwise just do roadside parking and walk a bit to the river/campsite. Basic toilet and shower facilities are available (male/female separated). Do not expect luxury. But water is strong for shower and the flush works. The campsite is well maintained, no garbage strewn around,  no funny smell, not much mosquito, no wild dogs/cats, no monkeys. It is good. But watch out for squirrels they'll eat any fruit left unsupervised. There are still other insects that bite like mosquito though. Crowds peak on Friday and leave by late Saturday afternoon because Johor starts to work on Sunday. Solar lights are placed nearby toilets, walkway and parking area. To see stars at night, walk further away from camp to avoid the lights. There are several spots where you can safely enjoy the waterfall cascades. Feel the water rush that massages your back. Get some nice photos. Water is relatively clear at the upper levels and lesser at the lower part of the river. Some areas are shallow and it is suitable for children. Camp right in front of the river. Awesome experience to relax while keeping an eye on your children and doing barbecue. There are lots of shade and  you can feel the cool temperature.

Title: Baba Nyonya Heritage Studio
Review: The Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum is a treasured cultural heritage site in Malacca's heart. It authentically recreates the lives of the Peranakan Chinese, a group that emerged from the long-term integration of early Chinese immigrants with the local Malaysian community. Formerly the century-old residence of the Zeng family, the museum was converted into a museum in 1985, to systematically preserve and display their unique architecture, furnishings, clothing, and everyday items. Guided tours offer insightful explanations of the social structure, religious beliefs, and customs of the Baba and Nyonya people, providing valuable insights into and understanding Malaysia's diverse cultural landscape.

Title: Baba Nyonya Heritage Studio
Review: In Malacca, which flourished as a hub for intermediary trade, we visited the homes of the Baba-Nyonya community, descendants of Chinese immigrants and local Malaysians. These residences, built in the Peranakan architectural style, reflect both tax-saving designs (such as narrow facades) and feng shui principles.The buildings feature long, narrow layouts, skylights, and inner courtyards—distinct characteristics of Peranakan architecture that also reveal the clever adaptations of the people who once lived there. Touring these homes offers a glimpse into their way of life and a chance to imagine daily life in those times.

I hope to have the opportunity to visit and compare them with those in other places.

Take the experience knowing you will be cared for in case of need.

Title: Borneo Cultural Village
Review: This is a must visit spot for learning all about the many tribes and traditions  as well as the different races of people that make up Malaysia. Located within a fruit orchard, guests can get a feel of how the early settlers of Malaysia made their livelihood as well as the native people of Borneo. Guests can take part in traditional games and experience how natives carried out their daily activities. The highlight of my visit was trying out the blowpipe and dancing the bamboo dance /magunatip dance. Guests also get to try their hand at cooking malaysian cuisine. The visit ended with a local buffet. Overall a great and affordable experience.

Title: Borneo Happy Farm
Review: Good natural environment with fun and nice interaction with animals. Place is well maintained and really appreciate the hospitality of the staff. However, wish they can improve on a few things to attract more people and be more sustainable in the long run.- Roads heading to and away from Borneo Happy Farm were small and rough- RM40/30 for Msians a bit pricey with more to spend for photo session, zipline, horse ride, animal feeding etc once inside. Even the buggy ride is not free and costs RM12 per person. All the extra charges feels a bit off putting, as if I'm in China. Wish for some free perks like free drinks during the hot weather but there aren't any...- Enjoyed the educational aspects of this trip but felt it's not enough (I want to learn more!) The speaker's speaker also not working during my visit. Pity her she has to speak loudly to get her voice heard..- Wish for more animals. Where are the birds and insects? Title: Botanical Gardens Penang
Review: I visited Penang Botanical Gardens on a weekday morning and found a peaceful, green space close to George Town. 😊Entry is free and the main gate has a small cafe for overpriced coffee and cold drinks. There is a small foodcourt too by the entrance.I walked the main path from the gate, past the lily pond and along the stream toward the quarry and secret garden, and the whole route is shady, easy to follow and full of birdlife. If you like bird watching this place is excellent. 😍I added the birds found in this area image to my review for you birdwatchers out there 😌A small stream with gentle falls runs through the park and there are lawns and benches for resting. Trails are signposted and some lead into longer hikes toward Penang Hill if you want to explore further. Wildlife sightings are frequent: I saw dusky leaf monkeys, long-tailed macaques, lots of birds and many butterflies.Practical tips: go in the morning for the best experience, bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens for birdwatching, and keep snacks zipped away because macaques can get bold 😅.The park map and the bird ID images I attached are helpful for matching what you see to names. Overall, the main walking loop from the gate to the quarry and back will give you the best variety in one visit and can easily take two to three hours if you stop and watch.Facilities are basic but generally clean, with public toilets near the entrance and limited parking. Bring water, sun protection and insect repellent for comfort.

Title: Botanical Gardens Penang
Review: The Penang Botanical Gardens is one of the most refreshing spots to escape into nature while still being close to the city. It’s a beautifully landscaped area with wide open lawns, shaded walking paths, and a mix of curated gardens and wild greenery.🌿 Nature & SceneryThe gardens are spacious and well-maintained, featuring a variety of plants including orchids, ferns, palms, and unique tropical trees. Some areas, like the lily ponds and fountain gardens, are perfect for a slow, relaxing stroll. There are also small waterfalls and streams, which add a natural charm to the setting. The Understorey Florarium is an interesting stop if you enjoy learning about local plant species.🦜 WildlifeAs you walk around, you’ll likely spot plenty of monkeys and squirrels. The monkeys can be cheeky, so it’s best not to carry food openly or get too close. Bird sounds fill the air, adding to the tranquil atmosphere.🚶 Walking & HikingThere are several trails that connect to nearby hills and forest areas, making this a good starting point for longer hikes if you’re up for it. Otherwise, the paved paths are comfortable for a casual walk, even with family or kids.🌸 AtmosphereThe overall vibe is peaceful, though weekends can get crowded with joggers, families, and tourists. Mornings are the best time to visit for cooler weather and fewer crowds.💰 Entry & AccessibilityEntry is free, which makes this an incredible value. It’s also accessible for wheelchairs and strollers in the main areas, though some trails are more rugged. Parking is available near the entrance.✨ OverallA must-visit in Penang if you enjoy nature. It’s not only a botanical garden but also a blend of manicured beauty and wild rainforest edge. Perfect for a walk, photography, or just to enjoy fresh air away from the city buzz.

Title: Botanical Gardens Penang
Review: A wonderfully natural and super lush tropical botanical garden.  There is NO  ENTRANCE FEE at the Penang tropical garden as well.Uniquely different from the equally excellent KL and Singapore tropical gardens.This garden is a more natural,  more lush, and not nearly as well  manicured garden  as either the KL garden or the Singapore gardens. That is precisely its charm!There are loads of trails  winding through various displays and presentations. Walkers, hikers, and  joggers seem to enjoy the multitude of trails.Monkeys are EVERYWHERE.There are displays of herb gardens, orchid gardens,  fern displays, aeroid trails, and much more.The original gardens were established in 1884 from an old quarry site, under the supervision of Charles Curtis, who was the first superintendent, making it one of the oldest botanic gardens built by the British in a colonial settlement.Penang Botanic Gardens is part of Penang Hill Biosphere Reserve, recognized by UNESCO as the third Biosphere Reserve in Malaysia listed in the World Network of Biosphere Reserve (WNBR).[2]Currently, 12-2024, there is construction of a cable car system taking place, which limits access at the very beginning of the road leading into the garden.Restrooms 🚻 are limited.Handicap doable in many areas. Title: Botanical Gardens Penang
Review: Awesome green lung space in Penang. It can get really crowded on weekends and public holidays. We went quite early in the morning by Grab and thankfully so. It was teeming and drivers were desperately looking for parking spaces. We got off near the gate and it was quite crowded inside too. Once you're in and walking there is ample space and the greenery takes over the senses.It is a beautiful space. Trees and plants from all over the world. Many are labelled quite well. There are benches and gazebos as well where one can rest and catch ones breath. The gardens are quite well maintained and the cleaners are already on duty early in the day. So are the monkeys. Food inside is a strict no-no with these mischievous little fellas on the prowl.The flowers are a sight to behold as were the lotus ponds. We will keep coming back regularly, if possible on weekdays. Fresh air is such a wonderful thing and so is this verdant space in Penang.

There were two dogs running around the garden too. Bathrooms were third world. Other than it being free, don't waste your time.

Title: Chew Jetty
Review: Chew Jetty, the largest and most famous of the historic Clan Jetties in George Town, Penang, is a fascinating UNESCO World Heritage site offering a unique glimpse into a traditional waterfront lifestyle. It is not a single floating structure, but a community of floating houses—or, more accurately, stilt houses—built entirely over the water on wooden piers. These rustic, interconnected wooden homes have been continuously inhabited by descendants of the Chew clan since the 19th century, creating a living, breathing village seemingly suspended between land and sea.Visitors can explore the long wooden walkway to witness this unique way of life. While primarily a residential area, the jetty has become a popular tourist attraction, with many ground-level rooms in the houses converted into small shops selling souvenirs and local treats.For those interested in the water perspective, boating is a popular activity. Tour operators often offer short boat rides from the jetty, providing scenic views of the stilt houses and the George Town coastline from the sea.The cultural and religious heart of the community is marked by its temples. There are two significant Chinese temples on Chew Jetty. The temple near the entrance is dedicated to the God of Heaven (Jade Deity), and another temple at the very end of the main jetty is dedicated to the Taoist Sea Deity, Haisen, to ensure good fortune and safe journeys at sea. While the primary temples follow Taoist and traditional Chinese folk religion, a prominent, striking structure adjacent to the Chew Jetty is the beautiful Hean Boo Thean Kuan Yin Temple, often referred to as the Floating Temple. While this temple is not physically on Chew Jetty, its stunning location perched right on the water makes it a major highlight when viewing the jetties from the coast or on a boat tour.

Title: Chew Jetty
Review: It was my first visit to Chew Jetty and totally loved it. I decided to visit during the evening as the sun was setting. The commercial shops were already closed or were closing up when I got there. It was not crowded at that time and I felt it was an enjoyable visit then. There were many houses and shops on stilts along the Jetty.Some tips:- As there are residents who live along the jetty, the visiting hours are from 9am to 9pm. There is no cost to visit Chew Jetty.- Evenings work out to be the better time to visit as it is cooler besides having lesser crowds then.- There is a chinese taoist temple very close to the entrance of the jetty. It is free to visit and it is a beautifully, well maintained temple. Worth checking it out. (I have a separate review for this temple).- It is not the longest or largest jetty but probably the most visited by tourists.- A visit to Chew Jetty without patronising the shops but to see and take photos/ videos, should take between half hour to an hour top. It is really up to you as to how long you would like to spend time here.- When visiting, always keep a lookout for motorcyclists as they may ride by you to get in and out of their residences on the jetty.This is definitely a must visit spot in my humble opinion. I fully appreciate why this is a UNESCO heritage site and just beautiful to spend time here.

Title: Chillax Paddy Field Sunset Biking
Review:
I had an absolutely fantastic time on this bicycle tour with Goh in the Balik Pulau countryside. The ride takes you through rice paddy fields and quiet country roads, ending at a beautiful ocean-side sunset viewpoint that felt truly special. Afterward, Goh brought me to a local hawker stall for a delicious Char Koay Teow dinner. 

What made this experience stand out even more is that it takes you to a part of Penang that most tourists would never see. Goh is born and raised in Penang and, as a university instructor, he brings a thoughtful and genuine perspective. You can feel that he does this out of passion and pride for his home, and that makes all the difference. On top of that, Goh takes great photos throughout the experience and shares them with you, which is a wonderful bonus.

This is a one-of-a-kind experience and I highly recommend it. Definitely add it to your Penang itinerary. 10 out of 10.

Title: Chillax Paddy Field Sunset Biking
Review:
Go with Goh!!!! This has so far been the highlight of my time on Penang Island.  Right from initially booking the tour and through to being picked up from my Hotel in Georgetown, Goh's communication was fabulous, keeping me informed of what the tour would entail, what I needed to brink with me and even letting me know to have a good lunch as dinner would be a little late due to the timing of the end of the cycling part of the tour (sunset of course ... oh and what a delight dinner was when we did sit down to enjoy it).  The tour itself was fantastic .. so fabulous cycling through the paddy fields to Pantai Malindo and finishing up to watch the sunset over the Malacca Strait before cycling back to the car to drive to a night market for a delish dinner.  
Goh is so easy to talk to and the commentary and information he provides is a great combination of interesting tourist info, fun facts and good to know stuff and personal insight.  On top of that he is a really good photographer .. I have a stack of great pics to post on the socials and of course great memories of a very memorable day.  Highly recommend.
PS Goh cycles at a leisurely easy to manage pace .. no issues at all with managing to stay on track .. literally.

Title: Chillax Paddy Field Sunset Biking
Review:
Everything that has been written in his reviews were exactly true. The whole journey was fun and great and worth every penny.

Mr. Goh said my visit was kind of NOT an ordinary day, there were less cars and bikers, few visitors and Mr. Goh is even shocked I seem to be unfascinated with the paddy field experience hehe (that is because we have lots of rice fields (Phillippines), and I kept on hurrying him to see the shore and catch the sunset...(sunset lover here). I told him i didn't joined my colleagues who went on to another tourist spot, because something is pushing me in this place and hoping i could catch the sunset... and oops the sun was too shy hiding in those low level greyish clouds. ouch...:D

Mr. Goh was very professional and friendly, though it was not a picturesque kind of day he patiently and creatively took almost hundreds of pics of me in every scenic way we could have. Heheh We both did a great job, i love all the pics you took (Thank you again) *_*

Mr. Goh also mentioned that those line up of mangrove trees were planted to prevent or minimised possible damage from another tsunami in the future. 

And yes, that is why it was NOT AN ORDINARY DAY! 

Little did I know i will be stepping in the land that i  have had once a promonition of. Even before Tsunami 2004 had occured, I had a warning in my dream about it. And i was helpless crying in tears watching and hearing that sad news i have no control over.. 

Somehow, God moves us mysteriously, it must be the reason why i chose Mr. Gohs listing over going with my colleagues instead. Indeed, God is still a God of restoration and healing. No situation is too far gone for God to restore, And this place was a proof of God's love, a beauty, a gratefullness beyond words can explain.

Thank you Mr.Goh for this wonderful experience. God bless you more.

It was a surreal and majestic kind of experience i would never ever forget.

Title: Chillax Paddy Field Sunset Biking
Review:
In one word, this experience was magical. And that was because of this amazing combination of the location, the activity and the most incredible host, Mr Goh. I would like to cover each one separately.

The location - it is at the countryside in an area called Balik Pulau. It is quite far from Penang City, from areas like Georgetown. It will take almost 45-50 minutes to drive down. But, the way is beautiful and it is worth it to travel this far for this experience. The area is full of paddy fields and sparse population. You get to experience the real countryside whereby you see farmers harvesting paddy.

The activity - it is an adventure like no other on bicycles. Mr Goh, takes you first to a cycle renting place. Here we chose 2 X double riding bicycles. One was for me and my wife. And the other was for my two daughters, 18 years and 10 years of age. My wife doesn't know how to cycle, but yet both of us managed beautifully. Yes, there is quite a bit of cycling to be done for almost 1 hour in total, but not continuously. With enough stops and rests. Only in the evening while coming back to the starting point after sunset, it requires quite a bit of cycling and you might get a bit tired. But, nothing's worth it without a bit of hard work and adventure. And this tour is worth everything. So, after picking up your bicycles, you are taken to the paddy fields to experience paddy harvesting. You cycle through a mix of concrete and gravel roads, but all easy to ride on. Mr Goh who accompanies you everywhere also on a cycle, will take many pictures of you with lovely backgrounds and great posing ideas. This lasts for almost an hour before you start moving towards 2 sunset points next to the sea. Here you have to do a bit of trekking and reach those end points like places which overlook the setting sun on the sea. It is beautiful. The sunset is wonderful to watch and experience. You spend another hour before you ride back to the starting point which takes about 20 minutes of non-stop cycling. Once you deposit back your cycles, it is dark already. Mr Goh then takes you for dinner at a local street food place which is fantastic. He rides on his motorbike and you follow him. It took us half an hour to reach the dinner place which is an area with full of food stalls and in between are many tables to sit and enjoy fantastic local food. Mr Goh does all the ordering after doing a check on your preferred diet. The fried kway teow is simply fantastic. And then the satay. And then the coconut apom. Finally you finish dinner and say your goodbyes to Mr Goh. Few things to keep in mind. The tour starts at 5 pm and finishes around 9.30 pm after which you have to drive back wherever you are staying. Please wear sports shoes. Also eat something before you start as you will feel very hungry in between the tour. Wear clothes which cover your body and protect you from mosquitoes. But wear light clothes as it is hot and you will sweat after all the cycling. Mr Goh will give you water bottles, mosquito repellent and cycle torches to help riding back after sunset.

Lastly about our host - Mr Goh. One word for him. He is such a wonderful person. Friendly, funny and always taking care of you. And to top it all he is your personal photographer and he will take hundreds of these fantastic photographs which he will later share with you on google drive. Never before in any tour did we get so many photographs of ours and each and every one is so good. That’s what makes this magical and builds a bond with him. You actually feel bad when you part ways. He is such a selfless person who takes care of you all the time and always working hard to give you a good experience. Our family only wants to say a BIG THANK YOU to him!

I would very strongly recommend that you do this magical tour with Mr Goh!

Title: Chillax Paddy Field Sunset Biking
Review: I had a wonderful evening with Goh! He is a sweet caring young man that genuinely wants his guests to have a great experience: not just on the tour, but in his home country. I’ve seen many sunsets but what I liked about this trip was that in no way was this a place of tourists (like me). It was an intimate secluded spot with local couples, families and individuals just connecting with others and nature. I felt honored and privileged to be a part of that. The biking part is not long at all: maybe 30 minutes total so if you are looking for a biking tour, this is probably not what you want. If you want to escape the crowded areas, drive out to the countryside, get some fresh air on a short bike ride, see an amazing sunset, get taken to a local hawker food and market and have great conversation, then you should definitely contact Goh!!

Title: Choley Kampung Warna Warni Kuala Perlis
Review: If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to step into a postcard that’s been left out in the sun a little too long—come visit Kampung Warna-Warni. You’ll find seven kampungs stitched together with bridges, murals, recycled art, and homes that look like they’ve been dipped in rainbow sherbet. Some are stunning. Others are, sadly, losing the battle against the UV rays. It can get quite hot, depending on the time of day—the kind of heat that makes you question why you’re not just watching a travel vlog from your sofa. Most locals stay indoors because of it, only coming out when it cools down.Don’t expect too many warm greetings—you might get a few curious looks, but that’s about it. It’s not that people are unfriendly; you’re simply walking through someone’s actual neighbourhood, and it feels like it. It’s a bit like Penang’s Clan Jetties, but rougher around the edges. You’re never quite sure whether the locals are pleased about the foot traffic or simply tolerating it.Parts of the village are well kept, while others clearly need some love, with pools of black, stagnant water filled with discarded plastic bottles and an unpleasant smell. What is undeniably beautiful is the view from the bridge connecting the village to the Kuala Perlis jetty—sweeping river views and a breeze in your face.There are a few stalls dotted around, and an open-air restaurant at the car park if you’re desperate for food or shade—nothing fancy, but you can grab some local snacks like shrimp fritters or dodol pulut hitam. Prices are fair, and the food hits the spot.Unless you enjoy slow-cooking yourself on foot, you can also pay RM35 and hop on a choley (a local motor-tricycle). There’s quite a lot to see, and it’s the easiest way to explore. The drivers know their way around and will point out interesting spots. Don’t expect National Geographic-style commentary—more like, “This aunty makes the best dodol.”It’s hard to make up your mind about this place. If Kampung Warna-Warni wants to be a proper tourist spot, it probably needs better upkeep—and perhaps a 7-Eleven or two—though I’m also not sure the residents would be too thrilled about their home being gentrified.

Review: 🌿 A Hidden Gem in Cameron Bertam Valley – Cozy Leisure Farm 🌄 My recent visit to Cozy Leisure Farm was nothing short of magical. Nestled approximately 1200m above sea level, the journey up the steep hill was thrilling in itself—an adventure that set the tone for the rest of the experience. The moment we arrived, we were greeted by crisp, cooling air and panoramic views that made the climb absolutely worth it. What truly made the visit special was the founder himself, whose warmth and hospitality were unmatched. He personally walked us through his estate and campsite, sharing stories of how he cultivated the land over the past 30 years. His passion was evident in every corner of the farm—from the flourishing avocado trees to the vibrant grapes, passion fruits, yellow golden fruits, and even robusta and arabica coffee plants. It felt like stepping into a living, breathing encyclopedia of tropical agriculture. The farm also features two beautifully designed camping sites, perfect for a weekend escape into nature. Whether you’re a seasoned camper or just looking to unplug, the serene atmosphere and fresh mountain air make it an ideal retreat. To top it all off, the owner served us a delightful fruit platter, showcasing the very produce grown on his land. It was a sweet and refreshing end to an already unforgettable experience. And for families with children, there’s even a mini zoo with rabbits and birds, adding a playful and educational touch to the visit. If you’re looking for a unique, nature-filled getaway with a personal touch, Cozy Leisure Farm is a must-visit. 🌱🍇🍍🐇🕊️

Rounded up with a lunch at the Asam Pedas restaurant.Definitely recommended if you like nature and some time away from the busy city life.

Title: Explore Kampung Baru with a Local
Review:
This tour shows you they way generations of Malay lived and still live today!!! This Baru surrounded by a huge concrete jungle! Yet its serene, simple and unbelievably quiet!! Fuad is 4th Generation still living in the Baru.  Fuad is a gracious, friendly and very laidback Malay!! We walked his Baru and stopped along the way to for some history.  Learned about why homes were built the way they are currently. Learned about families lifestyles.  This Baru is SURROUNDED by tall sky-scrappers yet it retains its culture and Malay simple style of living!  
The BEST was being invited into Fuads home. We “chilled” in his family home and learned about his personal lifestyle and about his family!  We were lucky enough to meet his father, who graces us with a few songs while playing the guitar!  We had some food in his home at his dining table as we chatted! Fuad is gracious, generous, funny, laid back down to earth, and humble!  After we left his home, we stopped by his place of worship and learned about the Baru religion.  After we stopped at a local streetfood vender and had some great satay!! 
My cell service was not working, so Fuad used his phone to order us a Grab ride back to our hotel.  This is the type of guy he is!!!
I highly recommend this tour if you want to immerse yourself into the real Malay culture!!

Title: Explore Kampung Baru with a Local
Review:
Air BnB experiences are a way for travellers to step into the shoes of a local and to experience their way of life for a fleeting moment. 

Fuad’s 3-hour experience of Kampung Baru delivers this and more. Essentially, it is an in-depth and personalised experience which is, at a visceral level, an experience which will transcend language, culture and religions. You will start the tour as strangers and leave as part of his keluarga (family).

Fuad is a 3rd generation resident of the kampung, and has witnessed first-hand the manner in which modernism has impacted the quaint kampung life. He will bring you through the kampung providing information and insights which no travel book will provide. My wife and I found ourselves snacking on freshly picked fruits - rambutan, guava and jambu, and were given a literal taste of life there.

The best part of this journey was to be given an opportunity to visit his home. There, we were welcomed by his wife, Kak Siti. We found ourselves spending the evening engaged in revelling conversations. We were also given an assortment of unique savoury snacks and kuihs, before we continued with the tour of the kampung. 

The evening ends with a dinner at nasi lemak wanjo, which is arguably thy national dish of Malaysia. The setting is no-frills, but the place is hygienic and the food is delectable. I will recommend the rendang ayam (chicken which is slow cooked in herbs and spices with a special coconut blend).

It was truly a memorable night and we can’t thank these wonderful people enough. Terima Kasih Fuad and Kak Siti.

Title: Explore Kampung Baru with a Local
Review:
We had a most unique evening with Faud, but the highlight was the impromptu musical jam session in his own home with his family, that made the meeting of two cultures so poignant and meaningful. I brought my Chinese friend from Shanghai, who was in Malaysia for the first time and having such a memorable experience in a traditional Malay home in Kampung Baru means she will always preserve this impression of Malay culture as welcoming, warm, and have this connection to it. And vice versa for Faud's family to be able to hear a Chinese national who can barely speak English, much less Malay, sing Chinese classics as she plays the family's piano, and feel her spirit through the vibrancy of her song. These are the kinds of cultural interactions that allow us to feel our common humanness, and are so necessary. Thank you to Faud for making this possible. Title: Gani Famous Pasembur
Review: 1st time to Gani Pasembur in Gurney Drive hawker centre on a Wednesday night.The hawker centre is busy and staffy as usual 😅Almost all hawker centre stalls practice self-serving. We need to order, pay, and serve our own food.The staff are very passionate.  welcoming and greeting customer who approaching their stall.All ingredients are fried. I chose 2 Taufu, 2 fried beancurd slices,  and 1 fried onion ball. Proceed for cutting and topping with cucumber & turnip (I ask for extra portion) and some sauce, then make payment and bring it back to our seats to enjoy it. My plate cost RM9.The sauce is not the traditional potato Pasembur sauce. It is more towards the Indian rojak peanuts sauce; it has some spiciness but more sweetness in it.The cucumber and turnips give some refreshing taste and bring down some greasiness. It is definitely the right decision to get extra portion of it.Although it is not the potato sauce Pasembur I prefer, but overall OK.

Overpriced.

Title: Gani Famous Pasembur
Review: Why this remains popular is a complete mystery to me. The commercialisation and mediocrity of the food quality cannot possibly justify the 3.8 star score. While the selection is extensive, many are “lazy & convenient” choices typical of yongtaufu and honestly cannot be considered suitable for pasembur. I mean when did store bought processed crab sticks, fishball and hotdogs become part of pasembur? The taste was bland even for the fried stuff and some were not even fresh (eg. sourish tofu).They really took their time lazily cutting up my selection and drenched it with the most shockingly red “kuah“! It almost looked unreal and artificial colouring was definitely used given the intensity. The diabetic inducing sauce was sugary syrupy sweet with just a hint of spiciness. Absolutely no kick or aroma. The only redeeming factor is the generous portion of shredded jicama and cucumbers.My cucur udang, two tofu, two potatoes, boiled egg costs RM16. Would not say it’s highway robbery but it comes pretty close. Would not eat here again. The pasembur on Lebuh Union nearby is by far more authentic, tastier and definitely a better deal.

These alternatives provide a better opportunity to support local artisans and experience genuine Sabahan culture.

Review: The Filipino Market in Kota Kinabalu is a wonderful place to visit.  It is divided into sections: handicrafts, fruits, native snacks and fresh seafood.  At night, a part of the market becomes a night food market.  The people in the food market are actually nice but can be pushy.  But no need to fear, just buy what you want.  Do not buy what you don't want.The set meals at the night food market are affordable. 35 MYR for 2 people.  You get 4 different dishes of shrimp, squid, fish and vegetables and 2 servings of rice.  It is really good for its price.If you order fresh seafood to be cooked, then it is very expensive.  You will be charged cost of seafood plus service fee.  One dish can already cost you 70 MYR.So choose wisely.  People are not dishonest, they can help you choose.  Ask them how much everything costs before agreeing.The night food market can be smokey. It is muddy when in rains.  If you are picky about places, this is not for you.  Personally, i like its charm.

Title: Jelita Ostrich Farm
Review: It’s a sad place where everything is run down and shabby. We came here hoping for a fun experience but it’s just a few ostriches and emus. They charge RM8 per person and give each a packet of dried corn kernels which you can use to feed the ostriches. When we were there, the goats and cows were back at their sheds so we didn’t see any of these animals. After 10 minutes of feeding the ostriches we walked over to a shack where a friendly Indian man started telling us about the ostriches. He was also selling ostrich oil derived products like hair growth spray and all purpose cream for skin. The shack was so decrepit and had seen better days. I left wondering why we don’t have higher quality standards for our domestic tourism? I didn’t feel I got any value from the visit!Update: Surprisingly, despite the sad state of affairs at the ostrich farm, the highlight of the trip was the ostrich oil that I bought. Title: Kampung Budaya Sarawak
Review: The show was excellent and the houses were fantastic. However at the time of this review, the largest and most beautiful structure (Bidayuh longhouse) just burned to the ground about an hour ago, along with the massive grand hall where real human skulls were kept. We just spoke to the village chief in that building a few hours before and he was great. We are all truly saddened by the loss, but at least we'll have the memories. Note, early reports say the blaze started in the great hall where a fire is always burning, smoking the skulls. Apparently it's bad luck not to keep them in the smoke. Title: Kampung Kuantan Fireflies Park
Review: It's a bit overrated. You need not be disappointed if you miss it. However,  if you have a lot of time available and curious to find out what the hype online is all about (like us :)) You won't be upset that you visited, but can't rule out coming back disappointed.Few tips:1. Get yourself mosquito repellent liquids prior to visiting (it is also sold there for RM 20 to 30) not so good, but does the job.2. Dress easy - this is not a boat or a ferry ride.. it's a catamaran ride. Be prepared for a bit of stretching and crouching.3. Carry a DSLR instead of relying on your phone. It basically boating in the night. You need something that can handle extreme low light photography.4. The life vests are available in plenty but smelly (carry a body spray or perfume) otherwise you're only thinking of the odour/sweat smells and not enjoying the experience - You will for sure thank me for this one when you're wearing the vest. (You can hit that like in advance ;))5. Most important - Cards not accepted, just ensure you have RM 50 available per boat of 4 adults6. Get there early, queue up outside the ticket counter. If not you'll end up in a long queue later.7. If you're in a group, split your team - Few can queue at the ticketing counter and the rest can queue up at the boarding area. So you don't end up queueing twice.The drive from KL is enjoyable, a mix of highways and fields/crops.Enjoy your trip!!!

Title: Kek Lapis Dayang Salhah
Review: Kek Lapis Dayang Salhah in Kuching, Sarawak, has earned its reputation as one of the city's renowned and highly recommended sellers of kek lapis, and it happens to be a favorite in my family as well. On this trip, I had the pleasure of introducing my friends to this cherished establishment.Our stay at the Hilton Hotel required us to cross the Sarawak River via a small boat, or sampan. Conveniently, the pier was just a stone's throw away from the hotel. The short five-minute journey came at the minimal cost of RM1 per person, making it an enjoyable experience in itself.After disembarking on the other side of the river, we embarked on a brief five-minute walk to reach Kek Lapis Dayang Salhah. Arriving late in the evening around 9:30 PM, we found that most of the cakes were already sold out.Our group decided to sample some of the cakes and planned to place our orders the next day. The prices here were considerably more affordable than those at the waterfront, and the taste was equally delightful, if not better. The butter-based kek lapis was priced slightly higher at RM25 per piece, while the margarine-based kek lapis cost RM15 per piece. For convenience, 5 to 6 kek lapis could be neatly packed into a small box that fit perfectly in a luggage bag. I ended up ordering two boxes.What truly stood out was their exceptional customer service. Kek Lapis Dayang Salhah offered delivery directly to our hotel, with no additional charge. We only had to pick up our orders at the hotel lobby. For larger orders exceeding 15 pieces, it's advisable to place the order a day in advance to ensure the cakes are freshly baked and promptly delivered.My personal favorite has always been the masam manis kek lapis, and I found it just as delightful as ever. Without a doubt, I'll be ordering from Kek Lapis Dayang Salhah again in the future, and I would highly recommend it to anyone seeking a taste of Sarawak's famous kek lapis.

Title: Kiulu Farmstay
Review: We showed up without being expected and they manage to host a visit for us in a very diligent way ..this is the nice part Because of the non expected visit no lunch was ready but that was king of our fault They organize a few activities - rice grinding , pipe blowing and we went on a short tour to the owner village. Nice but nothing extraordinary over 30 minutes. I had asked before how we will be charged and were told you will see upon arrival at the village. Warm welcome by the family with fruits, music and dance and photos. Then the owner asked st which hotel we stayed and looked at my wife’s bracelet and was preparing the move to charge us big time, all this with a big smile of course 125 ringgits for each person !! - we were 3. We paid as we did not want to create any concern and even though we appreciate we have a higher standard of living in Europe, this was just outrageous for Borneo (plus we had to pay for our own transportation). This guy is a crook , do not go there and better spend your money somewhere else. I am sure all is business is run the same way. Good thing we had better experience with other Borneo people who did not only see us as wallets on legs. So long.

Title: Kiulu Farmstay
Review: i have to admit that when i first found out there would be no mobile reception and TV i was worried on how to keep a 2 and 6 year old entertained! but i decided that i needed to breakaway from that connectivity and reconnect without these technology devices. upon reaching the area, we crossed a suspension / hanging bridge. the kids found that amusing. then when they descended from the bridge, they ran around like wild chickens. when we approached the fig tree i was actually impressed how compact yet complete it was. we decided to do half and half for food - cook and also enjoy the local dishes which could be ordered. we went to the river for a dip, fed the fish in the pond, played with the local musical instruments, did a slight trek in vain to find a buffalo (don't make promises you can't keep to kids - so i learnt). we found the village buffaloes bathing in mud and owh gosh the kids were ecstatic. at night, we had an early dinner. Helenna (who prepared our food) and Aryl (our guide) stayed on to play and chat with us and the kids. by 9pm, we called it a night. the area is so calming and it really did give me a sense of peace. would i return?yes. how would i vacay there again?with friends! Imagine having a private space all to yourself and friends, BBQing and just enjoying the night. Now there are only 2 rooms, but you can camps comfortable in the shaded area. I would also have done Quad Biking but didn't have enough time for that. breakaway and get away. here at the kiulu farmstay

Title: Kiulu Farmstay
Review: We came here in February. The place is located across the river, and this is a single accom hut in the farm - so you’re basically the only ones there - which is why it’s so cool! When we get there they had just finished preparing us lunch. The caretakers were awesomely welcoming and friendly. The hut is one of a kind, open-spaced kitchen with two bedrooms plus a toilet. The kampung meals were absolutely delicious I could still remember it till this day. At night it can get pretty eerie as there were no one else there in the viccinity but we had a Mr. Wexton who camped outside during our stay so he was always there to make sure we were OK. The river in front of the hut - superb! It’s not rocky like in Kolumpong or Tegudon and best thing is - the river is all yours for the entire stay. We enjoyed our stay here - it is one of a kind experience. No TV, wifi is weak, and there are bugs flying around especially at night so you may want to keep your sleeves long and bring a bug repellent. Get a full board package so you don’t have to cook your own meals plus you’re helping the community to earn some cash.

Review: Went during the Kaamatan Festival. It was packed with people and cars are parked dangerously outside the main road (which is not safe for the pedestrians especially for children and elderly). Anyway, here's what I liked the most, the handmade handicrafts, the traditional cultural longhouse (RM1.00 per entrance), the homemade delicacies like lihing, sikat, fish and fruit pickles ranging from RM10.00 and above (no free sample/food testing okay), the local vendors' agro culture products (sadly, I didn't see much of it, since the name of  'Kaamatan' means harvest clearly mentioned) but I enjoyed the Goat Milk Honey Ice Cream though (yummy *.^). For a first timer visit to KDCA during Harvest Festival, it will be a cultural shock, where you can see lots of 'pork' and alcohol stalls here and there plus the locals get drunk till morning (I wondered how the nearby neighborhood can sleep at night with the 'nightclub' noises) Thanks God it was a sunny day. For your information, the entrance fee (not on festival season) is RM25.00 for local and Foreigner is RM35.00. Here are my snapshots on the Kaamatan event itself *.^

Title: Koisaan Cultural Village
Review: Went there on the morning of 19 April.At 10plus in the morning, the sun was killing us.The cultural village tour was fruitful and we got nice experiences in it.We bought the ticket at the location. we think we were the first visitor to the compound on that day.We visited the various model houses of the natives.But the memorable peak of visiting this place will be the station tasting Lihing (glutinous rice wine), eating sago grubs (butod), learning to start fire and cook the butod, use the blowpipes, jumping onto the traditional trampoline and watching the traditional music being played on gongs and kenong.Our guide, a young lady (wished I could have asked for her name) was very pleasant and knowledgeable. We asked a lot of questions beyond what was seen onsite.The murut house is exciting as we have to cross the swinging bridge, to be met by the native from Murut on the other end.The sago grubs, or Butod is a MUST TO TRY!!Yes, initially the thought of eating a worm can really test ones nerves. But after overcoming it, the butod eating is actually pleasant and delectable.There is nothing unfamiliar with the taste, except for the fear of eating a worm.The butod personally for me tasted like fried egg. Especially the white part of the egg white which was fried with a bit of brown bits on it. Some said it tasted like fresh uncooked sweet corn.Because the flavour is familiar, I am compelled to say that I am definitely going to have more butod in restaurants around KK that serves them.I do recommend tourists to visit this place, even though the weather is not friendly enough. Because their hospitality is superb!Wishing KDCA all the best and will expand to have more native housing and share more of the native cultures and history with us. Will visit you again definitely!!??

Title: Kuala Sepetang Eco Tourism
Review: Stumbled upon this private tour service on Google Map while searching for activities to do in Taiping for a family trip. In contact personally with Mr. Khairul Salleh. Since it was a private tour service, time was flexible - which is a plus for a crowd with kids, trying to get ready on time!Mr. Khairul Salleh is very friendly yet professional, and very knowledgeable in regards to Kuala Sepetang and its neighbourhood.We took 2 trip packages: daytime trip around Kuala Sepetang & nighttime trip for the fireflies.Daytime Kuala Sepetang trip:90min boat trip along the river. We were shown around looking at the fishing industry, the mangrove forest & the coal factory. We landed at the 'Shell Beach' where the kids managed to collect various seashells washed ashore by the local cockle & shellfish industries byproducts. Then we stopped at the fish farm looking at tilapias, horseshoe crabs, pufferfish & mudskippers. Info sharing session by Mr. Khairul Salleh was very informative & interactive. I was very happy that my siblings & the kids were very happy getting involved throughout the trip. We ended the trip watching eagles feeding on the river. Magnificent! Oh, almost forgot the mangrove sapling release into the river with hope of everlasting green ecosystem for the future to enjoy & cherish!Nighttime firefly trip:Another memorable trip. One hour session watching fireflies amongst the mangrove trees flashing lights synchronously along the river. We were all in awe by Mr. Khairul Salleh's vast knowledge of the fireflies & the mangrove habitat, and reminded us how crucial & important keeping earth clean & green is to the sustainability of the ecosystem.All in all, we really enjoyed it & definitely would recommend it! Keep it up, En. Khairul!!!

Title: Kuala Sepetang Eco Tourism
Review: On 6.6.2025, our family embarked on a memorable river boat tour in Kuala Sepetang, Taiping that offered an enriching blend of nature, wildlife, and local culture. Tickets were reasonably priced at RM25 per person. We were the first group to set off that morning at 10:00 AM, joined by three other families about 12 people in total.The tour began with a warm welcome from the locals, who were enthusiastic and eager to share their knowledge. Our guide, a friendly and knowledgeable young Chinese girl, accompanied by an experienced boatman, made the journey even more engaging with fascinating stories about Kuala Sepetang’s history and environment.Our first stop was a floating fish farm, where we got up close with a variety of marine life, including crabs, puffer fish, and several other sea creatures. We had the chance to feed them and snap some close-up photos, making it a fun and educational activity for both kids and adults.From there, the boat took us along a peaceful stretch of mangrove forest. Gliding through the calm waters, we soaked in the beauty of the mangrove ecosystem an important natural habitat rich in wildlife and tranquillity.The final part of the tour was particularly exciting. As the boatman gave a few loud honks in the middle of the river, dozens of wild eagles appeared and began circling above us. Watching them glide and dive overhead was a spectacular sight perfect for photography and an unforgettable end to the journey.In summary, the river tour was an unforgettable experience that delighted the whole family. Between the close encounters with marine life, the scenic cruise through mangroves, and the incredible sight of wild eagles responding to the boat’s honking, it’s a must do activity for anyone visiting Kuala Sepetang. Highly recommended!

Title: Kuala Sepetang Eco Tourism
Review: Very educational boating tour along a river and highly recommended for family trips with kids as Mr Khairul patiently takes time to explain every detail about the places visited and the wildlife in the area. There are several stopovers made and the trip is not rushed as it is a private tour. You get to learn about the different types of fish farming, cockles farming, as well as the various types of boats used in catching different types of seafood. You also get a chance to view different types of coastal birds in the area. There is a stopover at a kelong where you get to feed the fish and also get a chance to hold puffer fish and horse shoe crabs. There is also a cool demo of archer fish hunting their "prey". There is even a "mini ceremony" for everyone to release mangrove seedlings in the river. The trip wraps up with watching the feeding of brahminy kites. You might want to prepare your cameras to capture the action of these kites swooping down over the river. Overall a truly wholesome experience and money well spent. We went over to Rasa Sayang seafood restaurant for lunch ( not part of the trip) as it is just a short walk from the jetty. Their food was great and very affordable. So a wonderful way to conclude your family execursion at Kuala Sepetang

Title: Kuala Sepetang Eco Tourism
Review: If Google tells you the ticket costs RM200, don’t panic. It’s actually closer to RM25. Some private charters may charge more, but the standard tour is affordable and easy to join. The boats are clean, the life jackets are in good condition, and the whole trip has a “choose your own adventure” feel. Some ads mention dolphin sightings, but don’t count on it—they’re seasonal at best, maybe even mythical. No one brought them up on our visit.What is on offer is a surprisingly rich view of river life. You’ll pass under the town’s iconic bridge while someone explains the different types of handmade boats. Then you’ll stop at a kelong (a floating fish farm)—part zoo, part classroom—where you might hold a horseshoe crab or gently touch a pufferfish. Kids get excited. Adults act cool. But everyone learns something, whether they admit it or not.The highlight is the eagles—and they don’t disappoint. They are trained and arrive when the boats do. Like clockwork, the sky fills with 20 to 30 pairs of wings. Rumour has it you get to feed them, but we didn’t on our trip. Still, they fly close enough for great photos—and even better memories.Most staff speak Malay and Mandarin. English varies depending on the guide. If your guide is Khairul, you’re in luck—he’s passionate, knowledgeable, and deeply respectful of the environment. The kind of person who makes you care about mangrove trees more than you thought possible.Local schoolchildren often help out with customer service. Some are enthusiastic, others clearly wish they were somewhere else. On the one hand, it’s impressive how capable they are. On the other, you hope they’re being treated well and not skipping school just to help tourists hold sea creatures. Either way, it gives a glimpse into the town’s effort to keep eco-tourism alive.It gets busy during peak times—expect long queues and less of a personal feel. Visit early or during off-peak hours if you prefer something quieter. Tours last around an hour to 90 minutes. Timings are flexible—or just loosely followed. Some slots are fixed, but others seem to leave when enough people arrive. It’s charming in a slightly chaotic, agak-agak kind of way.All in all, this isn’t a polished theme park—and it doesn’t try to be. It’s the whole kampung coming together to share what it knows, what it loves, and what it’s trying hard to protect. And if you’re lucky, you’ll leave with more than just pictures of pufferfish—you’ll leave with a new perspective.

Behind this is a café that serves food with bird nest. A few steps away from the café is another sales centre dealing with mainly organic cereals.On the ground floor of the swiftlet house, you can watch a video presentation of everything about bird nest and a mock-up of the swiftlet house. Title: Langkawi Eco Ventures (Mangrove Kayak Tour)
Review: Superb! Brilliant day with Sham who was so entertaining, enthusiastic and knowledgeable!!Booking process was really simple. We booked directly through WhatsApp (number on website).On the day, prior to arriving we received a WhatsApp from Sham explaining where to meet him.We only had one other guest on our tour. Sham explained that whilst he has worked in the industry for over 20 years he has only recently set up this company. Guest experience is very important to him therefore his policy is to keep group sizes small (max 10).We then took a speed boat into the Eco Forrest. The first stop was the bat cave which was fascinating. Sham took us through the cave and we saw the bats up close. (Beware the trouble making monkeys).After, we got back in the speed boat and headed to the floating restaurant where we picked up our Kayaks. Sham provided us with water and dry bags. The Kayaks were great quality included a back rest which was really welcome.We then Kayaked through the Mangroves for around 2 hours. We saw walking fish, lizards, grabs, a centipede, a viper snake, eagles and otters! Sham was so knowledgeable about all the wildlife and explained everything brilliantly!After a tasty lunch we were taken back via speedboat to the car park.I could not recommend Sham enough. The tour lasted 5 hours from 10am until 3pm and only cost around £35 pp which was amazing value.Strongly recommend! Thanks Sham!

Title: Langkawi Eco Ventures (Mangrove Kayak Tour)
Review: Had a fantastic time with Langkawi Eco Ventures and cannot recommend them enough! Our guide Sham was all in all everything you want in a guide: super fun, engaging, knowledgeable and well prepared. Overall did not know what to expect when booking the experience but came away feeling fulfilled by a good morning of learning!We started the day around 10am (there were clear instructions on how to meet the guide). We gathered and first took a boat to a floating platform which turned out to be a restaurant. There we already got the opportunity to get up close and personal with some of the marine life in the geoforest park, including horseshoe crabs and stingrays. After that we grabbed our gear, hats and water prepared by the guide, and explored the mangroves on kayak over a good 2-3 hours. The time absolutely flew by and while it may sound like a long time, we had ample rest stops where Sham shared his experience and answered our questions about the mangroves. By the end of the morning we had seen different types of marine life, learnt about the local monkeys, and saw several eagles! Around 1:30pm we had the opportunity to share lunch with the new friends made and even got lucky and snuck a visit to the Bat Cave nearby before we ended! The guide, boatmen and other members of the group were really friendly and outgoing.Would really recommend this company to go with, if you’re looking to do something to learn more about the natural environment in Langkawi and get some exercise in the meantime! Apply lots of sunscreen and wear clothes you don’t mind getting just a little splashes on.

Badan terasa sangat segar selepas berehat sambil mandi disini sebelum meneruskan perjalanan.Terdapat juga campsite disini jika ingin bermalam. Terdapat juga beberapa gerai jualan makanan ringan seperti lokching dan jagung. Untuk masuk, dikenakan cas rm3/kereta. If you are vegan, practice a more plant-based diet, or just plain curious about this Malaysian cooking experience, it is highly recommended :)

Title: Mah Meri Cultural Village
Review: I thought I could at least enjoy an experience in this place since one has to pay an entrance fee of RM30 for local tourists and RM40 for overseas tourists.The welcome drink was just iced cordial near the front desk. Each guest was given a weaved headgear to wear. There was not much of activities except watching one of the orang asli carving from a tree trunk (which was the only highlight). If you are expecting a dance or anything of that sort, there was none. Either there were too few tourists or it was too early (we were there at 11.30am)There was no guide to give you a personal feel of the lifestyle of the orang asli. You are practically on your own walking and entering the galleries (which you need to use your handphone torchlight to read the history, as the lighting was very dim).There were two ladies waiting near the cafe to teach tourists some simple weaving/origami to take home.To make it a little more worthwhile, I had my guests play "5 stones" at the cafe, and shoot seeds with catapults.It was at least educational and to see the unique and intricate carvings.

Title: Maklang Cafe by Ilham Ceramic Studio
Review:
Kafe comel ini terletak di Penarak, Kuah, Langkawi. Perlu masuk sedikit jalan kampung bertentangan TS Duty Free Chocolate Shop. Parking luas dan mudah diperoleh. Sebaik menjejak kaki ke dalam cafe, terus
terpegun melihat dekorasi dalamannya yang begitu mempesona. Kecil saja tapi tidak terasa sempit. Simple tapi menenangkan. Nyaman dan tidak panas walaupun cuaca panas terik. Ruangan dalaman juga sangat bersih kerana pelanggan perlu membuka kasut untuk masuk. Layanan dan sapaan dari owner membuatkan pelanggan terasa begitu dialu alukan untuk makan di sini. Beliau juga sedia membantu pelanggan memilih hidangan yang sesuai dari lembaran menu yang disediakan kepada pelanggan. Ulasan berkenaan hidangan yang ditawarkan di sini menunjukkan beliau sangat arif berkenaan setiap menu hidangan yang ada. Hal ini sangat membantu pelancong dari luar yang mungkin tidak tahu menu lokal seperti laksa atau cucur udang.

Kami memesan sepiring set cucur udang Mak Lang, minuman jus apple asam boi dan teh o ais. Kudapan kerepek ubi juga disediakan sementara menanti hidangan utama sampai. Cucur udang dihidang panas-panas dan kuahnya juga lebih dari cukup untuk hidangan 2 orang.

Rasa cucur udang juga sesedap rasa, cukup pedas dan masinnya. Tidak ada yang keterlaluan dari segi rasa. Kuah kacang juga sedap dan tidak terlalu pedas.

Dari segi minuman, jus epal asam boi memang terasa kepekatannya. Pure dan tidak terlalu manis. Terbaik tukang bancuh airnya.

Kaedah pembayaran yang disediakan juga pelbagai. Cash atau cashless. QR Pay, ApplePay, atau kad semua boleh. Sungguh memudahkan pelanggan.

Kesimpulannya, jika mahu mencuba aneka hidangan lokal utara Malaysia seperti laksa, mee kari atau cucur udang, datanglah ke sini. Layanan dari staf sangat mengalu-alukan, dan suasana persekitaran dalaman dan luaran cafe juga begitu mempesonakan.

Review: Malaysia Heritage Studios adalah destinasi yang sangat menarik dan berbaloi untuk dikunjungi, terutama bagi mereka yang ingin mengenal lebih dekat budaya dan warisan setiap negeri di Malaysia. Tempat ini menampilkan pelbagai rumah tradisional dari setiap negeri, lengkap dengan informasi yang disesuaikan untuk kanak-kanak yang bersekolah. Ini menjadikan pengalaman pembelajaran mereka lebih menarik dan interaktif. Setiap rumah tradisional disertai dengan sejarah dan latar belakang yang mudah difahami, menjadikannya destinasi yang sesuai untuk pelancongan pendidikan.Selain pameran rumah, terdapat juga aktiviti dan persembahan menarik yang boleh dinikmati oleh pengunjung. Review: The Malaysian Heritage studios is a pleasant place to visit and perfect for those who love taking pictures. Total Time spent was about 2 hours.

Similar to the Karyaneka Handicraft Centre in KL, each house contains furnishings, fixtures and works of art depicting the culture of each state or country.Located in Ayer Keroh, the Mini Malaysia & ASEAN Cultural Park showcases the country's 13 states represented with houses that actually look alike to the untrained eye (save for the Borneo house). However inside each abode is where the differences can be seen with life-sized wax dummies dressed in respective traditional costumes as well as local handicrafts. At the Mini Malaysia Complex there is also a model of an Orang Asli village."

Title: Mari Mari Cultural Village
Review: My visit to Mari Mari Cultural Village was one of the highlights of my trip to Kota Kinabalu. This place offers a beautifully curated and interactive glimpse into the diverse indigenous cultures of Sabah, all set within lush rainforest surroundings.From the moment we stepped into the village, we were welcomed warmly by our friendly and knowledgeable guide. The tour took us through several traditional houses representing different tribes — the Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau, and Murut. Each home was brought to life with demonstrations and storytelling, from fire-starting and tattoo ink preparation to blowpipe techniques and traditional rice wine processes.I especially appreciated the opportunity to try Kuih Penjaram, a sweet local delicacy made with rice and pandan — soft, fragrant, and delicious! We also learned about native crafts and even sampled food cooked in bamboo. The Murut longhouse segment was fascinating — rich with history, culture, and even a bit of dramatic flair.The surroundings were serene, with a peaceful stream running through the village adding to the charm. This wasn’t just a passive museum-style experience — it was hands-on, authentic, and respectful of the indigenous heritage.Highly recommended for anyone wanting to deepen their understanding of Sabah’s people and traditions. Allocate at least half a day, bring water, and wear comfortable shoes — you’ll be walking through the forest and up bamboo stairs. It’s worth every step!

Title: Mari Mari Cultural Village
Review: Yesterday’s visit to the mari-mari cultural village turned out to be an unforgettable journey through time. Surrounded by the echoes of the past, I was deeply moved by how our ancestors adapted and survived with such limited resources — their wisdom is nothing short of remarkable. Carl, our passionate Dusun guide, shared his culture with such depth and clarity that everything I’d once read in textbooks finally came alive before my eyes. It was a humbling and enriching experience that reminded me how much we can learn from those who came before us. Rasa macam ilmu dari buku teks daripada sekolah menengah akhirnya menjadi nyata. Terima kasih kepada semua orang kat sana menyampaikan segala penjelasan dengan begitu baik hingga setiap aspek budaya terasa hidup.

Title: Mari Mari Cultural Village
Review: We visited the Mari Mari Cultural village and great value for the tour, can very much recommend. I wasn’t expecting much food wise as a vegan but there was a decent selection of food in the buffet suitable for vegans and everything suitable had a vegetarian label as well as ingredients written out so I felt at ease and didn’t have to ask anyone if I could eat anything! The local food provided in the demonstrations was also accidentally vegan except for the bamboo cooked chicken rice, but the guide asked our group if anyone was vegetarian and to my surprise they had a chicken free option! Was very tasty and made my day they really thought about offering options which is not often on these kinds of tours. Would recommend to anyone interested to learn more about Borneo’s ethnic minorities

Title: Mari Mari Cultural Village
Review: Mari Mari Cultural Village is a unique place that allows you to immerse yourself in the rich culture of Sabah’s five main tribes: the Kadazan-Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau and Murut. Each of these tribes has its own unique history, traditions and lifestyle, which you can learn about during an interactive tour of the village. Visitors can see traditional houses, learn how to make fire with bamboo, learn about tribal tattoos and try local delicacies.Transport and accessibilityGetting to the village is relatively easy using the Grab app, which allows you to quickly book a ride from Kota Kinabalu. However, getting back can be more difficult – finding a driver in the area can often require a long wait. So it’s worth planning your visit in advance or considering an organised tour that includes round-trip transport.Is it worth visiting?Despite the minor inconvenience of the return journey, Mari Mari Cultural Village is a place worth visiting. It’s not just a museum, but a living space where you can experience authentic Borneo culture and get a feel for the old days. If you are interested in the history and traditions of indigenous tribes, this place will surely provide an unforgettable experience.

Title: Mari Mari Cultural Village
Review: I would agree that this is the "Best Tourist Attraction Non Nature/Man Made", as stated on their main website!Opted for the morning (10am) slot.The tourists are generally divided into smaller groups, or into groups per families led by a guide each group.Staffs were extremely cordial and welcoming. Our guide was Layren, who was fluent in English and Bahasa Melayu and spoke little Mandarin.The location is shaded by the tall forest trees, so there was no direct sun despite the timing of the tour and we found ourselves surrounded by enchanting nature, with birds occasionally calling out from the trees and some long wild lizards creep at corners of the walkway. We were safe from being bitten by any mosquitoes throughout the tour.Would, however, recommend to don light, cooling clothing as it’s still quite humid and a little smoky in some areas.The tour was enlightening and fun, as we got the chance to immerse ourselves into the lives of the 5 tribes, their distinct cultures, homes and even taste their snacks at their long-houses. Guests were welcomed to join in on activities such as their traditional trampoline called the Lansaran, give it a go with the “Sumpit”, a blowpipe weapon, take home a souvenir in the form of their artform “tattoo”, which looks similar to Henna ink and enjoy the cultural dance. Guests are also welcomed to the stage to join in on the bamboo dance.The buffet lunch spread is delightful and the drinks served are refreshing.Our small family went together in one group, consisting of 2 senior citizens and 2 toddlers. The steps are gentle and cater to the toddlers and senior citizens. Entering the long-houses, there are options for the traditional bamboo steps, for the immersive experience or the gentle steps. Everyone of us enjoyed the experience at Mari Mari Cultural Village! Definitely recommended!

Our guide, Mr Zul, did an excellent effort: guiding us through different houses and educating us on history in an entertaining way. One of the houses has a built-in traditional "trampoline-like" floor ! I am also impressed by the dances and musical performances. Beautiful smiles everywhere, and one can see they are just happy, kind and proud doing what they do. There is also a sense of peace and tranquility in the environment which I love. Anyway, my deepest respect for everyone who works to keep the Village alive. I really do suggest everyone to go visit and support the place. The knowledge and experience are just precious.

Title: Maria Kek Lapis Sarawak
Review: Original Cheese Kek Lapis = RM10.00Most of us would know of this Indonesian Cake known as "Kueh Lapis" but in Kuching, its known as "Kek Lapis". This is another Kuching Speciality. This is the type of Cake that really takes alot of patience to make. Just looking at the intricate layers upon layers and you can tell that alot of work is gone into the making.Kek Lapis in Kuching are usually sold in a Thick Long Slab and mostly range from RM8.00 to RM15.00 and up. And from most of the Kek Lapis shops I visited, the prices are more or less the same throughout.There are many Kek Lapis Shops around and I chose this one specifically because they have 2 Adorable Cats within! They're so Adorable they're really Enjoying Themselves, Sleeping and Manja all over the place.The Staffs here at Maria are also very Friendly with a Smile and I chose their Classic Kek Lapis which is something called "Original Cheese" Of course there are many more flavours to choose from. There are so many Beautiful Variations of Kek Lapis, it almost feels like you're touring an Art Gallery. They even have a Free Sample station so you can have a try which Flavour you prefer before you make your decision.For this Original Cheese Flavour, the thing that I noticed first was that it had a very Strong Cheesecake like Smell. The Actual Cake don't actually have any Cheese Taste though, which was a slight disappointment, but the Butter taste is Very Prominent. Its not the Super Buttery type of Taste, but you can definitely feel its presence here. Personally, I also thought it tasted just nice and not too sweet.After tasting this, now I understand why this is called "Kek Lapis" rather than "Kueh Lapis" because this totally doesn't taste like how you'd imagine it to taste. It really does taste more like a Cake than a Kueh. Texture is Soft, Sticky and Spongy, and I thought it tend to stick to my Throat often. This is perfect if washed down with some Tea or Coffee.RM10 for this size of Kek Lapis I feel is worth it just because of how much work it takes to make this.Personally, I don't know if this is really the Best Kek Lapis ever, but the Combination of the Friendly Staffs, and the 2 Super Adorable Cats is a Yes from me for Maria. I can recommend to come here if ya'll want to give Kek Lapis a try.Thanks for Reading. Come join my Facebook Food Blog: "A Solo Singaporean's Guide to JB Foods" to view the Full Review with Photos.

Review: Mira Cake House ( Cawangan Keramat).Sapa rindukan Kek Lapis Sarawak Mira boleh mai sini.... Bermacam jenis kek lapis boleh dibeli sama mcm Ibu Pejabat di Sarawak..The Sarawak layer cake, known as kek lapis Sarawak (meaning "Sarawak layer cake") or kek lapis moden Sarawak in Malay, is a layered cake from the state of Sarawak in Malaysia.This cake can be found almost everywhere in the Malaysian state of Sarawak. Usually Kek Lapis Sarawak will be served on special occasions. They are often baked for religious or cultural celebrations such as Eid ul-Fitr, Christmas, Deepavali, Gawai, birthdays and weddings.People in Malaysia practice an open house tradition during any festival day, and the modern layered cakes way be served almost everywhere in Sarawak.The Sarawak layer cake has its origin in a form of layer cake with various spices found in Indonesia called lapis legit or kek lapis Betawi (Betawi refers to Batavia, the old name of Jakarta).This spiced Betawi cake is thought to have derived from a form of European spit cake, which was made by the wives of Dutch administrators in Batavia during the colonial period and served during evening tea.It is believed that this type of spiced layer cake was introduced to Sarawak in the 1970s and 1980s by the Betawis from Jakarta. The Sarawak people then added new ingredients, flavour and colour that resulted in a new version of the layer cake being introduced and named as Sarawak layer cake. In addition, modern Sarawak layered cakes were inspired by Western cake-making in the early 1980s, later modern design to the traditional layer cake, along with new flavours were introduced.

Title: Monsopiad Heritage Village
Review: I took a Grab car here from KK and am so glad I did. For 65 MYR (international tourist rate) I was able to show up on a weekday around 10am and be assigned a guide to take me around the village for an hour and a bit. I get the feeling that on weekends or during peak season that booking in advance is advisable though.My guide spoke English and also doubled as a cameraman (he excelled at both). To list some, there's food tasting, starting a fire with bamboo husks, blow darts,  and also a dance performance. The whole visit takes a bit more than 2 hours.It is fairly simple to get to and from this place. We took a Grab from downtown KK, the drive is somewhere between 20-30mins, depending on traffic conditions. This is very convenient for those who decide to visit on a whim and do not want to join a tour group. Plus the communication from Monsopiad Heritage village is prompt via WhatsApp or their social media. So just check with them if you have any queries

Title: Murug Turug Eco Tourism
Review: A hidden gem place of Sabah, Malaysia. If anyone loves adventure, waterfall, or a short trek, they must visit this place. It's almost 50 km away from kota Kinabalu city. Grab/Taxi/ self driven car is available. But best to take a self driven car from kota Kinabalu.Must need to pre book through their website. But if you are foreign visitor, you can book through their given contact number on the website, as the payment option is bank payment.They have 4 packages. One can choose according to their choice, strength and health condition. We have taken Package B which includes 3 waterfalls. I mostly loved the second waterfall named Piolungan Waterfall.With the package, a guide cost is not included. Must need to take guide. Our guide was super friendly, caring and funny. His name was kungkum. Best guide, I have ever seen. Gossip with the guide, they will share lot of information about the trek, village, waterfall and local stories 😀Tips to visit there:1. Wear quick dry clothes, if you have plans to swim in the waterfall. Indeed, you can't resist swimming after seeing the beautiful waterfall. Once you put your foot in the cold water of the waterfall, you can't say no to swimming.Note: They have changing facilities and washrooms for both male and female. Not a posh one, not a low condition. Basic facilities.2. Bring hat, sunscream, raincoat for sun and rain protection.3. Must wear a trekking shoe or sandal4. Bring some light food if you want to eat food during the trek5. Bring waterproof gadget cover if you want to capture some close pictures with the waterfalls.6. Skip to go in weekend days, if you want to enjoy trek and capture your good picture.5. Last not least keep your trash with you.

Title: Murug Turug Eco Tourism
Review: A very beautiful scenery of waterfall 🤩...To come here you need to book through their website, no 'walk in' visitor. There have 3 package available...package A you will meet only 1 waterfall, need to walk 3 km roundtrip (suitable for beginner hiker)... Package B, you will be served 3 waterfalls, the trail take about  4 km (roundtrip), moderate hiking level. And for package C you will meet 7 waterfalls through 8 km trail, it is a challenging trail.All those trail, you need to have a guide for every 5 person. Though the package A very simple and easy trail you need to pay for a guide too. As we are beginner so we only dare to take package A (for starting, for survey the trail before we decided to take other package next time). Package A very easy but don't underestimate it. Please wear suitable shoes, as the trail can be slippery some time. From main point to the waterfall, you can walk leisurely, the path is only downhill all the way. but, to return back to the starting point, you need a lot of stamina because you have to walk uphill along the route.. for package A, pay for rm35 for a guide (apply for 1-5 hiker)

What I meant by that is the water levels was as high as the second time I went [Went for Package B the second visit]. The guides were friendly and helpful for my group members who was less outdoor-inclined. They do provide Maggi-cup noodles at the 5th Waterfall [Murug-Turug] - but you'd have to pay for it. If I'm not mistaken, 1 maggi-cup noodle was about RM4. You can even rent floats at the 5th waterfall to enjoy in the waters.Other amenities they provided - shoes for rent at the starting point - but mind you it is what we Sabahan calls - Kasut Adidas Kampung. They also provide free use of hiking sticks made of wood.You can opt for certificates at the cost of RM5 per person.All in all, the whole booking process was cheap, and absolutely had no hassle whatsoever.

Title: Murug Turug Eco Tourism
Review: Amazing experience hiking with my husband and our friendly guide Pastor Andrias. We took package C (8km), started walking just before 8am and finished before 1pm with a beautiful, refreshing swim stop at Murug Turug (although it was just 2 of us and guide, and I think we walked quickly and didn’t take many other breaks). Absolutely unbeatable rainforest waterfall and mountain views (80% in the shade which was a relief for those worried about heat and sunburn!). You can buy snacks and drinks at the start point. Quite challenging hiking and scrambling up rocks at times as well as a few places to wade through streams, but ropes provided where needed and should be a good level if you’re relatively fit and healthy! Really good value for money, and we had a great experience. Thankyou!
