My husband and I have done many cooking classes all over Asia and this is the first one we found really disappointing.To highlight the main issues:- the class is meant to be 3 hours. It actually lasted 4 hours, and the first 1.5 hours were just sat around a table with a weak ceiling fan with a lot of the time being Khalid showing us pictures from recipe books.- Khalid prepared all the ingredients in advance (amount, chopping etc). At times we were asked to identify ingredients, or do simple things like tie a knot in a pandan leaf which was not very engaging.- the ingredients were shared between the whole class and dished out by khalid so even though we had our own pans to make rendang curry, we were essentially just stirring the pan as khalid added the ingredients to the pan for us. We did have a little control over adding more water if needed, and we requested extra sambal- because the sambal was made by Khalid one portion for everyone to share there was not enough for everyone which meant people were asked to take some off of their plates to give to others, I've never seen something like this before- It was the same with the char kuay teow - but worse as this is a quick 4 minute cook so waiting for him to dish out each person's ingredients meant things got burned (eg. Garlic) and the taste was not good.- Khalid also took food from everyone's char kuay teow to "taste" but put it all on one plate for himself anyway so it wasn't that there was any individual feedback and he was the one who had added the ingredients and he also concluded there wasn't much taste. Not sure what the point of this was except that he didn't have his own portion of food to eat?- there was no air con in the kitchen where we were cooking, there was a fan but we couldn't have it on because the flame in the stoves were then affected meaning it was uncomfortably hot in the small kitchen. We were given room temperature water maybe an hour into the session- the session didn't seem well planned out, it was often jerky and felt quite chaoticKhalid seemed well intentioned and took some photos during the class and sent some recipes after also but I personally wouldn't recommend this class even though it is affordable

I prepared each dish and as we cooked Khalid discussed how to taste and know that the dish was developing well. We sat down to eat each of the six dishes. My only regret was I don’t have the biggest appetite. Khalid did however pack up the Banana Fritters which my partner devoured gratefully in the hotel room.It was a super afternoon and I cannot recommend Mypintu Plate and Khalid enough after the course Khalid gave me guidance on further reading and equipment that I can get to prepare the dishes that we prepared and even sent me photos and videos of me at work in the kitchen.Thank you Khalid and Mypintu Plate

Title: Natural Batik Village
Review: A Cultural Gem in Kuantan – Hands-On Batik Experience at Natural Batik VillageI visited Natural Batik Village located in Balok, Kuantan, Pahang, and it was a truly enriching and enjoyable experience!The location is spacious and wheelchair accessible, making it suitable for visitors of all ages and mobility levels. I had the chance to observe how Pahang-style batik (block printing) is traditionally made. The staff were friendly and welcoming — they explained the batik-making process in detail, which made the experience even more meaningful.After that, I explored the retail section where they sell a wide variety of batik fabrics, as well as batik clothing for men, women, and children, in many beautiful designs and patterns. Pahang batik has its own unique style, distinctly different from the batik found in Kelantan or Terengganu, which makes it special and worth discovering.One of the highlights was the DIY batik painting area outside, where visitors can colour their own batik block art and bring it home. This is a fun and creative activity, perfect for families or school groups.Overall, Natural Batik Village is a must-visit destination in Kuantan for anyone interested in Malaysian culture, traditional arts, or just looking for a meaningful souvenir.

Title: Nazlina Spice Station
Review: Nazlina took a booking at short notice for New Year’s Eve afternoon. We felt very lucky to have her teaching to our small family group. We went to an afternoon market and sourced fresh ingredients for our desired menu (she asks you what you want to make, so it’s worth having thought about this before the market and cooking class). We had returned from a hike directly to the class without eating and she bought us some food and recently made spring rolls by her and a previous class so we wouldn’t be hungry. Throughout the cooking she instructs the preparation and tells stories of her past which made for a lovely experience for all of us. She imparts lots of knowledge and tips around all the food and cooking also. You can make almost anything I’m sure from any local cuisine -she knows it all. We made vegetable spring rolls, Laksa (chicken and seafood/chicken), Sambal and sticky rice witch coconut topping as no ripe mangoes were available for mango sticky rice at the market. The sticky rice with coconut topping was incredible! I can’t wait to make it for guests! She can cater for vegan/vegetarian/non-seafood also but it helps to know this in advance for her and planning as her classes can be  bigger in numbers than 4. The cooking class is in her large  garden beneath a roof outdoors and is a lovely setting. Her price is competitive and very reasonable considering all of the above and the duration of the whole experience. Thank you Nazlina for the wonderful experience which I’m sure all 4 of us will remember forever.

Title: Nazlina Spice Station
Review: Nazlinas class was very interesting.We booked the class two days prior for 260 RM per person (05/24). Having to pay in advance (you'll pay additional 6% for using PayPal, no fees for cash) makes it a bit inconvenient for tourists like us.Because we usually cook vegetarian she changed the menu for us spontaneously and arranged with the 2 other participants! At the class, after us admitting, that we are omnivores, but simply cook veggie at home, she introduced some fish/ sea food into our menu. I would have preferred a full vegetarian meal, but didn't pay proper attention at the market to ask for this. Kinda my fault.We meet early in the morning for breakfast and a food market tour filled with street food. The whole group was already very full after that! Actually, the street food was too much to cook after, we felt not really hungry even after we had cooked our dishes - a bit sad, as this was my main goal of the cooking course.Afterwards we cooked our dishes in pairs. Not every participant does everything, which I usually prefer. This way, I didn't learn each step of the dishes as I was doing something else. I can imagine the bigger the group, the less you'll learn individually.Our food was rather simple, but quite tasty and unusual for Westerners. Nazlinas approach to salad was interesting and the Nasi Lemak was very tasty!

The locals were super friendly, the vibe was laid back and relaxed and extremely clean. After the tour we went to Nazlina’s kitchen and after a short overview of the dishes we were going to cook, prepared everything. We made everything from scratch and it felt amazing in the end to see the colorful dishes and taste the rich spices that we had prepared ourselves!! Nazlina guided us throughout the process, there was no rush, and everyone was very involved. What a wonderful experience, thank you so so much!

Title: Nazlina Spice Station
Review: My third trip to Penang and a another great day cooking with Nazlina. The market tour was great, Nazlina's knowledge of food is second to none , i was introduced to herbs and other ingredients i had never heard of let alone tasted. Who knew that the local ginger is so much more fragrant than the regular ginger we all know. Nazlina also takes you on a tour of the streets around the market showing you intersting spots and giving information about food and local culture. There is plenty of opportunity to ask questions.Nazlina has moved to new premises,  easily accessible with easy access for all. There are various cooking stations so just like before everyone can have a go at chopping ,slicing grinding and cooking. On this occasion we cooked outside under cover which was great on a hot day.Nazlina is a brilliant teacher and is very intuitive so will tailor tasks to your ability. A kind and  patient teacher ,Nazlina guided me through the process of making a spice paste for the chicken rendang using a traditional grinding stone and roller (batu giling).  It really is cooking from scratch,  it's authentic and lots of fun.Once all the dishes were cooked we got to sit and eat. We sat at a big table where we could  chat and enjoy the fruits of our labour. On this occasion we made fish asam  laksa , chicken rendang and a sweet called kuih kosui.For me a trip to Penang is not  complete without a cooking session with Nazlina. I will definitely come back to Penang and i will definitely book another cooking lesson with Nazlina. When you encounter someone so passionate about the food and culture of this amazing place its hard not to be infused with excitement.

The environment of the house was off-putting and it felt like we didn't belong. Naz never asked us anything about ourselves or tried to connect with us or teach us about malay culture. Basically we felt that all our efforts were not appreciated and that naz was generally unhappy and taking it out on us. We stayed 2 weeks when we intended 5. This is not what the wwoofing page is set up for and i do not recommend you stay/work for naz. We do not ever leave negative reviews but felt that we had to voice our opinion for the benefit of others. People should not be spoken to or treated in this was especially in a volunteer work atmosphere.Do not support the poor treatment of volunteers!. Look elsewhere for this experience as unless big changes are made to Nazalinas attitude and format this is not the place to receive this experience.

Title: Nohutu Ecotourism
Review: We arrived at Notuhu Ecotourism around 4:30 PM for a brief visit and did not stay overnight. The entrance fee was RM6 per person, which is quite affordable. Parking was easy and conveniently located near the entrance.The highlight of the visit was the stunning view of Gunung Kinabalu. Although the peak was partially obscured by clouds when we arrived, the surrounding scenery was still breathtaking. The temperature was pleasantly cool, making it comfortable to explore the area. The river water was exceptionally clean, cool, and fresh, perfect for a quick dip or just enjoying the natural ambiance.Facilities included well-maintained toilets and a small surau, which I used. The surau was modest in size, resembling a small chalet, but it served its purpose well. There is also a food stall on-site offering local snacks and meals, which added convenience for visitors.One downside is that the facilities provided for the RM6 entrance fee are quite basic, so I would rate the facilities themselves only 2 star. However, the natural beauty and peaceful environment more than make up for this.Internet connectivity was surprisingly good, allowing us to stay connected during our short visit.Overall, my first visit to Notuhu Ecotourism was a very positive experience. The combination of beautiful natural surroundings, cool climate, and clean river made it a refreshing escape. I look forward to returning for a longer stay to fully enjoy all the activities and the serene environment this ecotourism site has to offer.

Title: Nohutu Ecotourism
Review: Pertama kali datang ke sini. Persekitaran cantik. Staff mesra dan sangat membantu. Cuma ada tiga benda yang saya rasa perlu penambahbaikan.1. No telefon yang diberikan di laman rasmi Facebook dan juga di Google Maps. Sebaiknya letaklah no telefon staff yang berada di lokasi sebenar. Saya hubungi no yang disediakan untuk membuat tempahan. Sebab kami sekeluarga datang pada cuti umum. Jawapan yang saya dapat, boleh datang walk in sahaja. Bila saya ajukan risau pondok yang saya mahu ditempah orang yang sampai lebih awal dari kami, jawapan dari owner, "tidak juga tu".Pada hari kejadian, saya call owner sebab tidak pasti akan lokasi, tapi tidak berjawab. Nasib baik ada no di papan tanda di hadapan simpang masuk untuk saya hubungi. Bila sampai di tempat pendaftaran, saya tunjukkan gambar pondok yang saya mahu, staff maklumkan, itu adalah gambar lama dan pondok baharu di tapak tersebut telah ditempah orang selama 2 malam.Syukur masih ada pondok bersebelahan yang kosong. Memandangkan saya membawa warga emas, jadi saya mencari lokasi yang tidak terlalu jauh untuk turun ke gigi air.2. Jalan masuk ke dalam rasanya perlu penambahbaikan. Ada satu bahagian jalan tidak rata menyukarkan kenderaan untuk masuk. Memandangkan permukaan jalan di bahagian tidak rata tersebut diletak batu-batu sederhana besar yang agak licin. Kenderaan masih boleh masuk cuma akan sedikit was-was memandangkan perjalanan untuk sampai ke campsite sedikit jauh masuk ke dalam. Risau jika berlaku kerosakan kepada kenderaan akan menyukarkan perjalanan balik. Memandangkan tidak semua pengunjung datang dari kawasan yang berdekatan.3. Kemudahan bilik mandi dan juga tandas. Bilik mandi sangat gelap dan pintu tidak dapat ditutup dari dalam. Perlu ada bantuan orang pegang dari luar. Lantai pula licin. Ini agak menyukar dan membahayakan apabila membawa warga emas. Selain itu kalau boleh untuk tambah jumlah bilik mandi sedia ada bagi menampung kapasiti pengunjung daytrip.Selebihnya, saya sangat puji staff yang bertugas. Sangat peramah dan membantu. Pondok yang kami sewa ditinggalkan oleh pengguna sebelum dalam keadaan kotor tetapi staff dengan pantas bersihkan dan tukar plastik sampah baharu. Saya request untuk tambahan kerusi pun dihantar dengan cepat. Tempat cantik, bersih dan keadaan sungai pun tidak terlalu dalam. Anak-anak dan parents pun enjoy. Highly recommended untuk datang bersantai di sini bersama keluarga.Saya sertakan gambar no telefon staff yang boleh dihubungi untuk buat tempahan.

Title: Nomad Adventure Sdn Bhd
Review: Came here for some whitewater rafting but did not stay at the camp. Good website, responsive over email and lots of FAQs and guidance to inform you of the trip.Took my parents who are 60+ and had never been whitewater rafting before. We had a great time. Not the most challenging rapids but was still good fun with about 22 individual rapids in total.Depending on the river conditions it can take 30 minutes (heavy rains, fast flowing river) to 2hrs to complete the course with a 20min or so break in the middle for some drinking water and an apple. If the water is low it takes longer but is not as fun and the boat can get stuck. If the river is higher it's a lot rougher but over quicker! They advised the best time is around November to December if I recall for higher waters.Our guides were friendly and fun. They also provided lunch which was quite tasty back at the camp.The site is located in a small kampung and requires a lorry limo transfer (circa 30 mins) from the home base to the launch site. They provide lockers toilets and showers if neededWould love to come back to gopeng again for another round of rafting or perhaps some of their various other activities in the future.The guide also shares photos via WhatsApp free of charge which is nice. Good customer service!

Title: Nomad Adventure Sdn Bhd
Review: Our family of four had an absolutely fantastic experience with this company! In preparation of our trip, the information provided through 1 on 1 Whatsapp-contact was thorough and clear, which made us feel well-prepared for our adventure. Safety is clearly a top priority for them, and they went out of their way to reassure us following the unfortunate incident that occurred in November (not with this company!).Their flexibility was impressive; they arranged for an extra guide to join our white-water rafting trip with his family just a day in advance. This made it possible for us to have our trip, as their safety procedure calls for at least two boats for a trip so you can keep an eye out for each other. Before the trip, we were treated to a delicious lunch, which was a great start to our activity.The equipment provided was in good condition, and they took ample time for the safety briefing without compromising the fun of the activity. Their most important rule is to keep smiling, no matter what :-) (and they explain how smiling helps your safety!). Experiencing the river's strong current and colder temperature beforehand made us feel more comfortable and confident and allowed us to fully enjoy the rafting trip. Halfway through the trip, we were provided with drinking water and a healthy apple, and also enjoyed some time to play in the (calmer part of the) river.After the trip, it started to rain. They quickly arranged umbrellas for us so we could stay dry on our way back from a nice warm shower. The staff was all very relaxed and hospitable. The guide on the other boat took many photo's and video's on the trip and airdropped these to us afterwards.We also asked them where we could buy a congkak game as a souvenir from Malaysia. They went above and beyond to help us, sending tips via WhatsApp after asking around for us. Tips included the Sunday morning Fleamarket in Ipoh (recommended!) and a craft shop that unfortunately only sold newly made smaller sets. They even offered us their own if we couldn't find one. Unfortunately, we couldn't find a simple large wooden one, so we stopped by their place again (near Gua Tempurung) the next day. Although our guide from the previous day wasn't there, the ladies present knew about our request and had just been discussing where to buy one. Soon after, we walked out with a beautiful wooden congkak game (and a great story of how we found our souvenir) and some great lunch recommendations (Ipoh Curry Bread Bun!) and cave temples to visit.The staff were incredibly friendly and went to great lengths to ensure we had a wonderful (and safe!) day. Our son had been there before with his schoolcamp and had had a wonderful adventure too! Highly recommended! Would love to go back again and enjoy some of the other activities they offer (ziplining through a cave sounds cool!).

Title: Nomad Adventure Sdn Bhd
Review: We came here as a group of 23 to kayak and stand up paddle (SUP) down the kampar river. The place is very easy to find using Waze or Google maps, despite being about 10 minutes off the main road into a kampung area. The compound itself is huge; comprising of a welcome area, canteen, and cabins. It's generally easy to park too. The guides were very professional; the briefings were clear and thorough. The river itself was very beautiful. The water was chilly, and the river cut deep into the forest - making you feel like you were far far from civilization. We travelled about 9km downriver (not much paddling required and the river was very calm) before getting picked up at the end and shuttled back to the starting point. Lunch was provided and the food was good too. Highly recommended. I'll definitely be back to do this again in a smaller party. Big groups are no fun because you have to keep stopping in order to keep everyone together.

Walking through these charming lanes, you’ll discover art that blends history, culture, and daily life in Penang. Every corner tells a story—whether it’s playful, nostalgic, or thought-provoking. The area is easy to explore on foot, and you’ll also find local cafés, shops, and street vendors nearby. This mix of heritage buildings and vibrant art makes Penang Street Art one of the top things to do in George Town. It’s a cultural experience you simply cannot miss if you want to capture the true spirit of Penang.

Title: Penang Street Art
Review: If you’re in Penang, a walk down Armenian Street in George Town is an absolute must for art enthusiasts and culture seekers alike. The area is a vibrant blend of history and creativity, with its iconic street art installations perfectly complementing the heritage architecture.The murals, many of which were created by Lithuanian artist Ernest Zacharevic, are an essential part of Penang’s charm. From the playful “Little Children on a Bicycle” to the wistful “Boy on a Motorcycle,” these artworks are not just paintings—they’re an interactive experience. Watching people pose creatively with the murals adds a delightful energy to the street.Beyond the murals, the area is alive with local businesses—boutique cafes, craft shops, and quaint galleries—adding depth to the cultural experience. It’s also worth exploring the hidden corners, as some of the lesser-known artworks and graffiti gems are tucked away in quiet alleys.Tip: Visit in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Comfortable shoes and a camera are essentials. If you’re here during the festive, visiting at night will have really nice light installations accompanying you too!Whether you’re here to soak in the art or enjoy the vibrant street life, Armenian Street truly encapsulates the soul of Penang. A stroll here leaves you inspired and deeply connected to the island’s cultural heartbeat.

Title: Restoran Selera Nogori
Review: Overrated, only word to sum up this joint. The reason we went because we googled place to eat in seremban and saw this. To our dismay, this is nothing more than canteen food with plenty more choices. You can taste that the food is mass-produced with little attention to quality. So...It's like...the more dishes the better, and people here just flock to this place. It's called selera negeri but there are Thai style chicken, butter prawn, to name a few - so its just a mashed-up food place with no unique offering to warrant high rating for my review. Its unlike several places we been to,  ie Haslam or Capital Cafe in KL that offer you tasty home made cooking with several noteworthy dishes like their kerabu, or petai sambal or even omelette.The place is stuffy and congested and hardly any space for you to walk. Service? Don't expect any friendly smiles here. In fact the servers keep on asking you to move aside with their stern faces as there's always one behind you carrying plates, glasses etc. Rice is free of charge, but of course its been built in the entire food price. I'm sure if I just eat a plate of rice with fried egg I won't be charged just rm1, or will I?Be prepared for smoke attack on you clothes or hair - there's smoke coming from the grill fish station into the shop and people who refuse to understand that smoking in enclosed area is prohibited.

The gift shop was beautiful, offering everything from elegant keepsakes to playful souvenirs. My daughters especially loved the free popcorn samples from the café and had fun exploring the interactive exhibits.It was a well-balanced mix of culture, hands-on learning, and fun for the whole family. Many thanks to Ilyas for including this stop in our tour. It was a hidden gem we might have otherwise missed. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Kuala Lumpur, especially with kids.

We wholeheartedly recommend this tour. Thank you, Kash! 🫶🏼

Title: Sky Ladder Pineapple Farm, Port Dickson
Review: 🍍MD2 Pineapple Plantation Visit – Negeri SembilanSweet pineapples, yes—but it was the interns who left the deepest impression.This MD2 pineapple plantation in Negeri Sembilan produces exceptionally sweet fruit with the signature low acidity of the variety. But what truly made this visit memorable was meeting the group of dedicated young interns running much of the operation behind the scenes.They came from across Malaysia—Sabah, Pahang, and beyond—bringing not just geographical diversity, but a shared spirit of commitment. Many are students pursuing agriculture-related studies, and their decision to intern far from home speaks volumes about their drive.Despite the tropical heat and long hours, they were energetic, articulate, and generous with their knowledge. From explaining soil prep to walking us through the science of pineapple enzymes, they handled it all with the kind of clarity and professionalism you might expect from seasoned guides.One of them even introduced me to gac fruit, a strikingly red superfruit grown onsite, sharing its nutritional benefits and harvesting process with quiet enthusiasm.In short, this was not just a plantation visit—it was a masterclass in what happens when youth, learning, and land come together.Highly recommended for anyone keen to witness Malaysia’s next generation of agri-leaders in action—oh, and yes, the pineapples are absolutely worth the trip.

Title: Sky Ladder Pineapple Farm, Port Dickson
Review: Skyladder farm is a mainly a pineapple plantation area but they do have few others fruits. We saw passion fruit, kedondong and of course, the special "Gac" fruit.They do have farm animals as well. My kids love it - they get to see up close some turkey, goose and ducks.We bought 1 ripe Gac fruit- was told is very nutritional (10 times more caretenoid than tomatoes) and good to try it.The staff is friendly and they provide briefing on the plants in the farm and also help to take pictures. I was told these people are actually uni grad doing their internship here. Hence, they're quite knowledgeable.Unfortunately we didn't get to see much pineapple as most of the fruits has been harvested. Well, we get to taste the chill pineapple juice which was very refreshing after visiting the farm.The only caveat was that only very small section of the farm is open to visitor. I was told by the friendly owner they have plan to open more section of the farm by end of the year .

Title: Sky Mirror Sekinchan
Review: We made a rather spontaneous dash to Kuala Selangor one rainy evening—departed KL around 7pm and reached just an hour later, umbrellas at the ready and spirits still high. The goal? To catch a glimpse of the famed fireflies, one of Kuala Selangor’s most magical nighttime spectacles.A word to the wise: the best time to visit is between 7 and 8pm. Any later and you risk missing the show, as the fireflies start to dim their glow and call it a night. Timing, it seems, is everything when dealing with nature’s own fairy lights.Now, if you’re lucky and time your trip just right, you might also witness the enchanting blue algae phenomenon—where the water lights up in a surreal neon blue glow. It’s like the sea threw a rave and forgot to invite the humans. But do note, this only happens during high tide and certain months, with June being the most likely candidate.Each experience—fireflies and blue algae—has its own dedicated boat tour, and we went with Jet Sky Mirror Kuala Selangor, a name that’s built a solid reputation in these parts. The boats are well-covered (a blessing in unpredictable weather), and the crew clearly prioritise safety and know-how, which is always reassuring when you’re out on the river after dark.Tours are reasonably priced at RM35 for adults and RM30 for children (local rates), though foreign visitors can expect a slightly higher fare. The ride lasts about an hour—just long enough to soak up the serenity and take a few “ooh and ahh” photos without overdoing it.All in all, it’s an experience that blends nature, wonder, and a touch of adventure. Just check the tides, keep an eye on the clock, and let Kuala Selangor do the rest.

Title: Sungai Lima Pulau Ketam Eco Tour
Review: Sungai Lima, nestled on the quieter side of Pulau Ketam, offers a refreshing escape from the bustling main village. Unlike its more commercialized counterpart, Sungai Lima embraces a laid-back, rustic charm that immediately puts visitors at ease. The moment you step off the ferry, you're greeted by a slower pace of life, where the rhythm of the tides dictates daily activities.The primary draw here is undoubtedly the tranquility and the immersive experience of a traditional fishing village. Stilt houses, painted in various shades and adorned with drying nets, line the waterways, creating picturesque scenes perfect for photography. You can observe local fishermen mending their nets, children playing on makeshift jetties, and the occasional boat ferrying goods – a genuine slice of local life.Dining options are simpler but authentic. Fresh seafood, caught just hours before, is the star of most menus. Don't expect fancy restaurants; instead, anticipate homely eateries serving up delicious, unpretentious dishes. While there aren't many organized activities, the joy lies in wandering the narrow wooden walkways, soaking in the peaceful atmosphere, and interacting with the friendly locals.Accommodation is basic, often guesthouses run by families, providing a no-frills but comfortable stay. It’s ideal for those seeking a quiet retreat, a digital detox, and a chance to experience the unvarnished beauty of Pulau Ketam. Sungai Lima is a gem for travelers who appreciate authenticity over tourist traps, offering a genuine glimpse into Malaysian coastal village life.

Title: Talula Hill Farm Resort
Review: Stayed here with my parents for one night and it was a wonderful experience. The resort is about a 15-minute drive from Kluang town, surrounded by peaceful and spacious greenery. Staff were very friendly, and there were complimentary activities like pebble drawing, visiting the vegetable garden, and feeding the sheep. You can call for free buggy service to travel to different places in resort. We got “picnic breakfast” which they deliver your breakfast (everything in picnic basket) to doorstep and you can just grab a picnic mat they provided and eat outdoors. Breakfast was amazing — very generous portions for three people, plus two large bottles of milk and orange juice. The Wi-Fi was surprisingly strong, and during check-out, we even received fresh vegetables from their garden. The room was clean and well-equipped with towels, toiletries, umbrella, iron, hangers, kettle, coffee and tea. Toilet and shower were separate, though the shower area was small with few hooks. The room had both aircon and a fan, but the fan couldn’t be adjusted. If the weather is clear, the night sky is full of stars, and in the morning you can catch the sunrise from the café side. A perfect place to stay for a night to relax and recharge.

Title: Talula Hill Farm Resort
Review: I always wanted my little one to experience a farm stay but still have some luxury. This place definitely offers this! The main building is right on the hill and a distance away but the staff is always ready with a buggy to fetch us around. Grabfood is allowed to be delivered to reception. Cafe food can be a bit pricey but portions are big and the food is good so it’s worth it! Our favourite is the pan seared salmon with cream sauce. Thank you for such a fun stay! Mosquitoes and bugs are expected but we managed.

Title: The Art Attic
Review: An art gallery disguised as a souvenir shop: intricate jewellery, hand-painted ceramics, delicate textiles, and postcards so beautiful you’ll want to send one to yourself. The location is perfect, tucked near Gaya Street, with a post office nearby so you can send those gorgeous postcards on the spot.On paper, it’s brilliant - local artists and handmade souvenirs. But it’s not really for the locals. And the price tags reflect that. Sabahans might stop by, admire the work, but chances are they’ll walk out empty-handed. Even some tourists feel the sting. A budget-friendly section wouldn’t hurt. Stickers, small prints, little things that don’t make your wallet cry. You see them in art markets, so it’s not impossible.The staff are friendly and fluent in English and Chinese, which makes life easier for tourists. No pushy sales tactics, just quiet smiles. But it’d be great if they knew more about the artists - who they are, what makes them special. Even a simple write-up could make all the difference. At a glance, the pieces have that polished, mass-market “Malaysia” look - bright, colourful, and safe. With a little tweaking, this place could be a true cultural landmark rather than just a pretty (and pricey) shop.

Title: The Backyard Glamping Cameron Highlands
Review: My son wanted to experience the trending glamping stay.I booked a night stay here for RM210.00, which is a couple tent. My son brought his own sleeping bag to sleep in.There are 3 types of tents : 2 unit of each family, couple and single tents. And priced at RM250, RM210 and RM120 respectively with added surcharge of RM30 on weekend, school and public holidays.I was advised by the opeartor to park within the compound of Ad Diniah school. As soon as I arrived and parked my car, I inquired about the parking payment and a school teacher told me to leave and not park my car there. I asked the Glamping operator and he told me to park at the roadside. It was really irresponsible of them to just brush aside security and safety problems of the car park. The roadside is pretty narrow and so, I decided to leave my car in the school compound.To reach the glamping site, there is a 30m hill hike with hand rails to assist.The glamping site also offers a DIY Steamboat set with added cost on service and rental of fire pit.Once there, we were told of the only toilet to use and some tips on staying in the tent. We had the farthest tent at the site and quite a walk to the toilet. The toilet was smelly and totally inadequate. We had to share that one toilet with the other tent dwellers. It is really disgusting.There is not much of activities to do here. The terrain in beautiful. I was hoping to do some hiking and some high or low rope activities here. But none is available here. It would have been great, though. None of the dwellers took the DIY steamboat, either.And early the next morning at about 8.30am, the  opeartor came by the tent and cleared the rubbish and waited to clean it. We actually had until 12 noon to check out. But, I felt like we were being chased away. We quickly packed our things and left.I find that glamping is not for me, especially on the issue of dirty and distant toilet. The absence of activities at the glamping site is also another frustrating issue.

The operators explain one by one to all atv/utv riders. N also giv you a free complimentary boat ride. The startdard rm80 per pax(adult) pricing involves a relatively easy 40mins off road ride thru the surrounding ladang sawit. Route difficukty is suitable for fetching kids 4 and above, but cautious is required. Its by far the easiest n newbie friendly atv route ive experience frm my few times of atv ride. Be sure to wear cool long sleeved clothing, or arm covers, sunblock n insect repellent is great too. A small bottle of water per rider would be sufficient for the ride.
